rounds.proof_sketch: blockDim.x=256 → 8 warps → warp_maxs[0-7] written, warp_maxs[8] uninitialized. Mutation causes lane_id=8 to read warp_maxs[8] (garbage) instead of -FLT_MAX. Garbage value is outside input value control.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation causes the kernel to read from warp_maxs[8], which is uninitialized shared memory (only indices 0-7 are written by the 8 warps). The content of this uninitialized location cannot be controlled through input tensor values—it depends on GPU runtime state. In practice, this location consistently contains values that don't exceed the true maximum (likely very negative or zero), causing bitwise-identical results across all 187+ test rounds. This is technically undefined behavior that happens to be benign in this environment.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable through value changes. The mutation reads uninitialized memory at warp_maxs[8] which is outside the influence of input tensor values. Would require changing block_size or dim2 to alter the warp count and boundary condition semantics, which violates the fixed-shape contract.
rounds.recommendations: Add explicit initialization of shared memory arrays (e.g., `warp_maxs[lane_id] = -FLT_MAX;` before __syncthreads) to eliminate undefined behavior and make such mutations more easily detectable through consistent incorrect results.
